## Problem

Open Brain has explicit graph tables, but no eval proves when graph links improve retrieval or guards normal search against graph-noise regressions.

Sprint: #265.
Paired with: #267.

This issue is paired with the graph retrieval implementation issue. The implementation must not be considered ready unless this eval gate exists and passes.

## Scope

- Add a deterministic relational retrieval fixture for Open Brain.
- Seed entities/links where the answer is not recoverable by normal keyword/vector text alone.
- Add a graph-family recall test with graph retrieval disabled vs enabled.
- Add a normal-query no-regression test where graph retrieval is a no-op.
- Add namespace leak tests for graph traversal and hydrated rows.
- Add archived-link/entity exclusion coverage.

## Acceptance criteria

- Fixture includes at least 20 relational questions across Open Brain-native relations such as `depends_on`, `blocked_by`, `implemented_by`, `decided_by`, `supersedes`, `duplicates`, `contradicts`, `mentions`, and `relates_to`.
- Relational recall improves materially with graph retrieval enabled.
- Non-relational query results remain unchanged or within an explicitly documented stable tolerance.
- A graph link in an unreadable namespace cannot affect returned rows.
- Archived links/entities cannot affect returned rows.
- The eval can be run locally and in CI without live Open Brain or external services.

## Validation expectation

- Focused eval/test command for the new fixture.
- Existing `bun test` / typecheck still pass.

## Non-goals

- Do not implement the retrieval arm here unless needed for test harness shape; this issue may land as skipped/failing scaffolding only if paired PR sequencing requires it.
- Do not add LLM-based relational parsing.
